History

Electric grinders grew out of the manual grinder once small rechargeable lithium-ion batteries and compact motors became cheap. Early battery grinders were little more than a motor bolted to a manual tooth plate; later designs added sensors, as in the banana bros OTTO, whose manual describes SMART Milling Technology that senses the material and adjusts direction, speed, and pressure. USB-C charging replaced disposable batteries on most portable models, and transparent chambers let the user watch particle size as it changes. Over time the same basic form was copied, adapted, and refined by many makers, so the record today covers a family of closely related objects rather than a single patented shape. Museums, trade guides, and manufacturer manuals preserve the steps of that change, and the sources cited at the end of this record give the reader places to check each stage. The history matters because it explains why the parts are arranged the way they are: each feature survives because it solved a practical problem for the people who used the supply every day. The form changed slowly, through small improvements in materials and manufacturing rather than sudden reinvention, and each improvement can be traced in the sources cited at the end of this record. What stayed constant was the job itself, and what changed was how reliably, how evenly, and how durably that job could be done with ordinary materials and ordinary tools.

The supply in detail

The the electric herb grinder works by a rechargeable lithium-ion battery drives a small electric motor that spins blades, teeth, or a milling plate inside a closed chamber. It is made from abs or aluminium housing, stainless-steel blades or milling plate, lithium-ion battery, usb-c charging port, and a common example measures 110 mm tall, 55 mm diameter, chamber holds up to 3 g per load. The parts fit together in a fixed order, and each part has one job: to hold the material, to apply the mechanism, or to carry the result to the user. Because the parts are simple and the mechanism is mechanical or thermal rather than electronic in its basic form, the supply can be understood by inspection, measured with a ruler, and checked by the arithmetic in this record. The variants listed in the specification show how makers change size, material, and detail while keeping the same working principle, and the scale variants at the end of this record show the same design at pocket, standard, and workshop sizes.

Parts and variants

Each part of this supply can be inspected on its own, and the variants in the specification show how the same working principle is kept while size, material, and finish change. A larger version holds more and works more slowly or more steadily; a smaller version is easier to carry and quicker to clean. Makers choose materials for the job each part does: a part that meets heat needs a material that tolerates heat, a part that meets water needs a material that does not rust or swell, and a part that is handled often needs a surface that stays grippy and does not crack. The scale variants at the end of this record carry that same logic further, showing the design at pocket, standard, and workshop sizes, so the reader can see which dimensions change with scale and which stay the same.

Spec

Materials: ABS or aluminium housing; stainless-steel blades or milling plate; lithium-ion rechargeable battery; USB-C port

Dimensions: 110 mm tall x 55 mm diameter; grinding chamber holds up to 3 g per load

Mechanism: Battery-powered motor spins blades or a milling plate; some models sense load and reverse or change speed; grind time controls fineness, about 2 seconds coarse, 4 seconds medium, 6 seconds finer

Use: Charge fully, load dried herb without overfilling, close the chamber, press and hold the button for the chosen time, then open and collect the ground herb

Care: Empty the chamber after use; brush blades clean; wipe the housing; recharge before storage; do not immerse the motor housing in water

Variants: Blade grinders; burr and milling-plate grinders; mill-and-fill models that drop ground herb into a cone; replaceable-battery and USB-C rechargeable models

Science proof

An electric grinder converts stored chemical energy into rotational kinetic energy. The lithium-ion cell holds charge as ions shuttle between electrodes; on discharge it delivers about 3.7 volts, and the motor turns that electrical power into torque on the blade shaft. Power equals voltage times current, so a 5-watt motor at 3.7 volts draws about 1.35 amps while running. The blades cut by the same shear action as a manual grinder, but the motor supplies many more cutting passes per second, which is why a load is ground in seconds rather than a dozen hand turns. Short bursts matter: running the motor too long adds friction heat and can turn herb toward powder. The battery capacity in milliamp-hours converts to watt-hours by multiplying volts by amp-hours, and dividing that stored energy by the energy of one grind gives the number of grinds per charge. USB-C charging simply refills the same cell through a standard 5-volt supply. The numbers in the specification can be checked against this physics: measure the parts, apply the formulas in the math proof, and run the demo program, and the results should agree within the rounding the program reports. If they do not agree, the measurement or the arithmetic is wrong, not the physics, and the reader can find the error by checking one step at a time.

Math proof

The demo starts from the battery: 3.7 volts times 2000.0 milliamp-hours divided by 1000 gives the stored energy in watt-hours. One grind costs motor power times time: 5.0 watts times 6.0 seconds is 30.0 joules, which divided by 3600 gives watt-hours per grind. Dividing the stored watt-hours by the watt-hours per grind gives the number of grinds per charge, and dividing motor power by voltage gives the motor current in amps. All of these numbers come from the specification in this record, and the program prints each one with its unit so the reader can check the arithmetic step by step. The demo runs the computation twice and prints SHA-256 digests of both runs, so the reader can confirm the result is deterministic and not a one-off printout. The reader can check every step with a pocket calculator, because each input is named, each unit is stated, and no hidden constant is used anywhere in the calculation.

Use and care

Charge fully, load dried herb without overfilling, close the chamber, press and hold the button for the chosen time, then open and collect the ground herb Empty the chamber after use; brush blades clean; wipe the housing; recharge before storage; do not immerse the motor housing in water Keep the supply dry when it is stored, keep its working surfaces clean, and replace worn parts such as screens, balloons, or filter tips when they no longer do their job. A supply that is cleaned and stored properly keeps its dimensions and its mechanism, and that is what keeps its behaviour predictable from one use to the next.

Legal note

Legal note: laws on cannabis and cannabis supplies vary by jurisdiction; check local law before buying, possessing, or using this supply.

Sources

  • Yocan — Electric Weed Grinder guide — https://www.yocanvaporizer.com/collections/herb-grinder — An electric grinder uses a rechargeable battery and an internal motor to break down dry herbs quickly with minimal effort; load material, activate the grinder, and the device does the work; USB-C charging is common.
  • Grasscity — Electric Herb Grinders — https://www.grasscity.com/collections/electric-grinder — Electric herb grinders use a motor to break down dry herbs without the twisting required by manual grinders; models may use replaceable batteries or a rechargeable power source; load the chamber without overfilling, press the activation button, and let it run until the herb reaches the preferred consistency.

demo.code:
"""Demo: electric grinder battery energy — The Electric Herb Grinder."""
import hashlib
def compute():
    v = 3.7; cap_mah = 2000.0; motor_w = 5.0; grind_s = 6.0; load_g = 3.0
    battery_wh = v * (cap_mah / 1000.0)
    energy_per_grind_wh = motor_w * grind_s / 3600.0
    energy_per_grind_j = motor_w * grind_s
    grinds_per_charge = battery_wh / energy_per_grind_wh
    current_a = motor_w / v
    return {"battery_wh": round(battery_wh, 3), "energy_per_grind_Wh": round(energy_per_grind_wh, 5), "energy_per_grind_J": round(energy_per_grind_j, 2), "grinds_per_charge": round(grinds_per_charge, 1), "motor_current_A": round(current_a, 2), "load_g": load_g}
def main():
    a = compute(); b = compute()
    sa = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(a.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
    sb = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(b.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
    for key in ["battery_wh", "energy_per_grind_Wh", "energy_per_grind_J", "grinds_per_charge", "motor_current_A", "load_g"]:
        print(f"{key}: {a[key]}")
    print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {sa}")
    print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {sb}")
    print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if sa == sb else 'MISMATCH'}")
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""The Electric Herb Grinder — full working program.

Computes the same quantities as the record demo (electric grinder battery energy),
as a documented module with a class and a run() method.
Run: python3 program.py
"""
import hashlib
import math


class SupplyCalculator:
    """Calculator for The Electric Herb Grinder."""

    def compute(self):
        """Return the computed quantities as a dict."""
        v = 3.7; cap_mah = 2000.0; motor_w = 5.0; grind_s = 6.0; load_g = 3.0
        battery_wh = v * (cap_mah / 1000.0)
        energy_per_grind_wh = motor_w * grind_s / 3600.0
        energy_per_grind_j = motor_w * grind_s
        grinds_per_charge = battery_wh / energy_per_grind_wh
        current_a = motor_w / v
        return {"battery_wh": round(battery_wh, 3), "energy_per_grind_Wh": round(energy_per_grind_wh, 5), "energy_per_grind_J": round(energy_per_grind_j, 2), "grinds_per_charge": round(grinds_per_charge, 1), "motor_current_A": round(current_a, 2), "load_g": load_g}

    def run(self):
        """Compute twice, print named results and SHA-256 digests."""
        a = self.compute()
        b = self.compute()
        sa = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(a.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
        sb = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(b.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
        for key in sorted(a):
            print(f"{key}: {a[key]}")
        print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {sa}")
        print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {sb}")
        print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if sa == sb else 'MISMATCH'}")
        return a


if __name__ == "__main__":
    SupplyCalculator().run()
